msContents.summary: Anonymous commentary on prayers, with additional quoted commentaries

msItem.title: Commentary on Prayers
פרוש התפלות
Perush ha-tefillot
msItem.note: This commentary by an anonymous author contains quoted sections of other works, including those by Joseph Kara (ff. 101r-111r, 114r-142v; probably also ff. 168r-180v, 206v-233v), Eliezer ben Nathan of Mainz (on the New Year liturgy; ff. 111r-114r), Rashi (on piyyutim; ff. 114v-160r), and Jacob Tam (f. 161). Ff. 206v-233v also incorporates additions by Solomon b. Samson.

The names of many other authors are quoted; these include Joseph ben Samuel Tov-ʿElem (Bonfils), Samuel ben Barukh of Bamberg, David ben Sheʾaltiel, Eleazar ben Judah of Worms, Benjamin of Canterbury, Jacob Nazir, Ephraim ben Jacob of Bonn, Meir ben Isaac Sheliʼaḥ Ẓibbur, Meir of Lisieux, Samuel ben Ḳalonymus and Ḳalonymus ben Yehudah.

supportDesc.condition: F. 1r is heavily stained and the text, which has been written by a later hand, is no longer entirely legible.

handNote.p: Copied by four hands. The first hand copied ff. 1v-105r (until the first line of the second column), and ff. 161r-249v. The second hand copied ff. 105r-133v (from the second line of the second column), ff. 143r-150v, and ff. 250r-270v. The third hand copied ff. 134r-142v, and ff. 151r-160r. The fourth hand, which may have been that of a later owner, copied the final quire (ff. 271-278).
The second scribe ruled the pages using plummet and hard point interchangeably; the other scribes ruled only with plummet.

decoDesc.p: The sections copied by the first scribe contains simple, geometric line fillers, abstract designs composed of dotted lines next to catchwords, and scalloped borders and fleur-de-lis extensions around some of the enlarged initial words. The scalloped borders on ff. 1v, 2r, 9r are drawn in red ink; all of the other drawings are in black ink.
The sections copied by the second scribe is largely undecorated, apart from three small rudimentary drawings of shofarot which illustrated the adjacent text (f. 132r).
The sections copied by the third scribe contains semi-abstract flourishes in black ink along side margins, and drawings of flowers that fill small gaps in the text.

bindingDesc.p: Dark brown leather with rough, pronounced grain over paper boards; blind-tooled decorations on both upper and lower boards. On the spine, a damaged paper slip bearing the printed number 10[7]3; the number 170 has been painted in white.
bindingDesc.condition: The leather covering the boards has been damaged in many places and has been repaired using dark brown leather with finer grain. Two clasps now missing. Many wormholes on the leather covering ther lower board: these are found also on the final folios (from f. 170 onwards) but not on the inner side of the lower board, indicating that the boards themselves were later replacements.

provenance.p: On f. 160r, a late-medieval owner who added a piyyut at the end of the commentary on the Rosh ha-Shanah liturgy signed his name as Aharon ben Mordekhai אהרן בן מרדכי.

During the late-sixteenth century, the manuscript was in the possession of Yuda ben Nathan Leib of Koblenz יודא בן נתן המכונה ליב קובלענץ, as attested by his ownership inscription (within a decorated frame) on a fragment of a leaf which is now glued to the pastedown at the end of the manuscript, as well as his records (in a mixture of Hebrew and Yiddish) of the births of his children as well as several deaths in the family between the years 1558-1572 on f. 279r.
On f. 279v, Nathan ben Yoʾel נתן בן יואל records that he inherited the book from his nephew, Mosheh ben Mosheh משה בן משה.

history.acquisition: It belonged to the library of David Oppenheim (1664-1736), which was purchased by the Bodleian Library in 1829.
